name: Julius LeMoyne
role: President of the LeMoyne Cattle Co., of Washington, Pa.
bio: Julius LeMoyne of Washington, Pa., visited the Bad Lands in June 1884, when the Cow Boy described him as the leading cremationist in the United States, owner of the country's only crematory, built by his father. He headed the LeMoyne Cattle Company, whose 500 high-grade heifers were driven from Glendive to its home ranch on Tepee bottom in July 1884, and was himself a breeder of Short-horn cattle and Berkshire swine. He wrote to the paper in support of the local stockmen's association and in March 1885 on the number of bulls a herd needed, and in October 1885, as president, decided to keep the LC herd on its range for the winter. In 1886 the paper printed notice of the company's reorganization as "The LeMoyne Cattle Co., Limited," a Pennsylvania partnership.
